topic.title: Naming Conventions
topic.description: Standard conventions for naming in Java

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Naming things in Java isn't just about creativity - it's about clarity! Let's master the rules that make your code speak for itself.

• Why naming conventions matter in Java
• How to name variables, methods, and classes correctly
• Common mistakes to avoid (and how to fix them)

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're organizing a toolbox. You wouldn't mix up screwdrivers and wrenches with random labels - you'd use clear, consistent names so you can find what you need instantly. Java naming conventions work the same way!

Java has simple rules to make your code readable:

• **Variables & Methods**: Start with lowercase, then camelCase for multiple words
  -  `studentName` (good) vs  `StudentName` (bad)
  -  `calculateTotal()` vs  `CalculateTotal()`

• **Classes**: Start with uppercase, then camelCase
  -  `StudentRecord` vs  `studentRecord`
  -  `BankAccount` vs  `bank_account`

• **Constants**: ALL_UPPERCASE with underscores
  -  `MAX_SIZE` vs  `maxSize`

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Class names use PascalCase with each word capitalized (e.g., ComputeArea)
Variable and method names use camelCase starting with a lowercase letter (e.g., totalScore)
Constants use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE with underscores between words (e.g., MAX_SIZE)
Package names use all lowercase letters (e.g., java.util.Scanner)
Consistent naming conventions make code easier to read and maintain

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Naming conventions make your code readable and professional. Variables/methods: `lowerCamelCase` | Classes: `UpperCamelCase` | Constants: `ALL_UPPERCASE`. Practice by fixing bad names in existing code.

questions.question: According to Java naming conventions, how should a class be named?
questions.explanation: Java convention uses PascalCase (also called UpperCamelCase) for class names, where each word starts with a capital letter (e.g., MyClass, StudentRecord).

questions.question: How should constants be named according to Java conventions?
questions.explanation: Java constants are conventionally named using ALL_CAPS with underscores separating words (e.g., MAX_VALUE, PI, INTEREST_RATE).
